title: Cache cannot reliably cache None results
reasoning: Cache.set accepts Any values, but Cache.get returns None both for misses and for stored None values. The get_or_compute methods treat value is not None as the only cache-hit condition, so a compute function that legitimately returns None is recomputed on every call even though the cache contains an unexpired entry. This breaks the generic cache contract for a valid Python value and can create repeated expensive calls or repeated side effects.
reproduction: Call cache.get_or_compute('k', lambda: None) twice. The second call enters the miss path again because get('k') returns None for the cached value.
recommendation: Separate miss detection from value retrieval with a sentinel or internal lookup method that returns entry presence independently of entry.value. Preserve public get behavior only if callers depend on None-as-miss, but make get_or_compute use the unambiguous internal path.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included CacheManager tests only cache string values and assert misses return None; they do not cover storing None or compute functions that return None.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add sync and async get_or_compute tests where compute_func returns None and assert the function is invoked once while subsequent calls return None from the cached entry.
